capture_alias.reason: scripts/viz-evidence.sh decides the pane has started by matching the literal string 'rataflow-view' in the pane's visible text. With the frozen path in the command line, that literal appears in the shell's own echo of the typed command, so the script captured the half-typed command line and lost the TUI. Giving the frozen bytes a second absolute path whose name does not contain that literal makes the script's own wait condition fire on the app's header instead. The bytes are identical: shasum -a 256 of the alias equals the frozen hash above, and every manifest records that hash.

spec_alias.reason: same shell-echo race, second half: the absolute case path is ~130 characters and its typing alone outlasted the capture. The alias keeps the command short; each manifest's spec_sha256 still equals the sha256 of the case spec it points at (verified per view below).

tie_breakers_considered: Density (tie-breaker 1): E=8 over N=9 is E≈N, so this is not a mesh or a fabric — the fabric family would demand double-arrowhead redundant targets the source explicitly refuses to draw ('missing hop proves nothing'; no spine/leaf invented).

Bus + disconnected worlds (tie-breaker 2): the /29 looks like a bus, but the source states every membership edge as member -> gateway ('same /29', 'free in /29'), so there is no bus splitting once; placement-planes was considered and rejected on that direction fact.
Identifier/qualifier content (tie-breaker 3): decisive. Coverage of addresses, ports, AS numbers and uncertainty markers is the hard part here; layout is easy (three shallow chains/star).
Motion (tie-breaker 4): the source shows no motion at all (a probe result, a NIC inventory), so the diagram is static — which also rules out lifecycle-machines.
